definitions: To raise a sensitive or difficult subject for discussion.
To open and start using the contents of a bottle or other container.
To pierce (a cask or barrel) to draw out liquid.
To turn (a ship) so that it presents a side to the waves and is in danger of capsizing.
examples: He was afraid to broach the subject of his salary.
They broached a new barrel of ale.
The whaler broached the whale to extract the oil.
The small boat broached in the heavy seas.
